items.title: Wendell Brunious interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Neal Hefti wrote some unbelievable string parts on there [Clifford Brown with Strings].

ctx.x: If you had to make a short list of trumpet players that every aspiring student should listen to, and really listen to, who would they be?

Okay. My first thing is whenever someone comes to me and says they want to study jazz, they want to try to play jazz trumpet, the first thing I tell them is go out and buy “Clifford © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-

Brown with Strings,” and I’m going to give you a free lesson. That’s always my deal. Because Clifford Brown displayed, on that CD, record, tape, whatever you have of it, how to play melody. Every song on there is a ballad. And Neal Hefti wrote some unbelievable string parts on there. And Clifford Brown just played the trumpet the way it’s supposed to be played. I mean he’s breathing, his accents, and just he knew when to swell a note or when to be really quiet. And you know like when he did “Embraceable You,”…
